samples.summary: Flat foldout styling removes the only visual cue that a note contains collapsed content, slightly widening a content-concealment surface in shared notes
samples.evidence: The `.note-details` border/background and the bold `.note-summary` are dropped (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css:241-252), leaving a collapsed foldout indistinguishable from an ordinary paragraph apart from a 0.7em '▶' glyph (lines 272-279). In a workspace- or share-link-shared note, a collaborator can hide arbitrary body text (altered terms, instructions, links) behind what reads as plain prose, where the previous boxed treatment made hidden content obvious. Impact is limited to reader deception — the folded body is still escaped markdown and cannot execute — so this is hardening/UX judgement, not an exploitable flaw; I could not construct a privilege- or data-exposure chain from it.
